cards.back:
Not happy. The prefix un- means not.
Bahasa Indonesia: tidak senang
Example: The unhappy boy lost his favourite toy.
cards.say: unhappy. Not happy. The prefix un means not. The unhappy boy lost his favourite toy.

cards.back:
Not kind. The prefix un- means not.
Bahasa Indonesia: tidak baik hati
Example: It is unkind to laugh at someone's mistake.
cards.say: unkind. Not kind. The prefix un means not. It is unkind to laugh at someone's mistake.

cards.back:
To undo a knot. The prefix un- means to reverse.
Bahasa Indonesia: membuka ikatan
Example: Please untie the rope from the boat.
cards.say: untie. To undo a knot. The prefix un means to reverse. Please untie the rope from the boat.

cards.back:
To write again. The prefix re- means again.
Bahasa Indonesia: menulis ulang
Example: I will rewrite my story with better words.
cards.say: rewrite. To write again. The prefix re means again. I will rewrite my story with better words.

cards.back:
To do something again.
Bahasa Indonesia: mengulang
Example: Please redo your sums and check them.
cards.say: redo. To do something again. Please redo your sums and check them.

cards.back:
To play again.
Bahasa Indonesia: memutar ulang
Example: We can replay the video from the start.
cards.say: replay. To play again. We can replay the video from the start.

cards.back:
To have a different opinion. The prefix dis- means not.
Bahasa Indonesia: tidak setuju
Example: I disagree with you about the answer.
cards.say: disagree. To have a different opinion. The prefix dis means not. I disagree with you about the answer.

cards.back:
To not like something.
Bahasa Indonesia: tidak suka
Example: I dislike loud noises at night.
cards.say: dislike. To not like something. I dislike loud noises at night.

cards.back:
To go out of sight.
Bahasa Indonesia: menghilang
Example: The rabbit seemed to disappear into the hat.
cards.say: disappear. To go out of sight. The rabbit seemed to disappear into the hat.

cards.back:
To spell wrongly. The prefix mis- means wrongly.
Bahasa Indonesia: salah mengeja
Example: Check your work so you do not misspell words.
cards.say: misspell. To spell wrongly. The prefix mis means wrongly. Check your work so you do not misspell words.

cards.back:
To give someone the wrong idea.
Bahasa Indonesia: menyesatkan
Example: The old sign can mislead travellers.
cards.say: mislead. To give someone the wrong idea. The old sign can mislead travellers.

cards.back:
To look at something before others see it. The prefix pre- means before.
Bahasa Indonesia: pratinjau
Example: We saw a preview of the film.
cards.say: preview. To look at something before others see it. The prefix pre means before. We saw a preview of the film.

cards.back:
Not possible. The prefix im- means not.
Bahasa Indonesia: mustahil
Example: It is impossible to count all the stars.
cards.say: impossible. Not possible. The prefix im means not. It is impossible to count all the stars.

cards.back:
Not able to be seen. The prefix in- means not.
Bahasa Indonesia: tidak terlihat
Example: Air is invisible, but we need it.
cards.say: invisible. Not able to be seen. The prefix in means not. Air is invisible, but we need it.

cards.back:
Taking care. The suffix -ful means full of.
Bahasa Indonesia: berhati-hati
Example: Be careful when you cross the road.
cards.say: careful. Taking care. The suffix ful means full of. Be careful when you cross the road.

cards.back:
Not taking care. The suffix -less means without.
Bahasa Indonesia: ceroboh
Example: A careless mistake made him lose a mark.
cards.say: careless. Not taking care. The suffix less means without. A careless mistake made him lose a mark.

cards.back:
Giving help.
Bahasa Indonesia: suka membantu
Example: The helpful boy carried the box for me.
cards.say: helpful. Giving help. The helpful boy carried the box for me.

cards.back:
Not able to help yourself.
Bahasa Indonesia: tak berdaya
Example: The baby bird was helpless in the rain.
cards.say: helpless. Not able to help yourself. The baby bird was helpless in the rain.

cards.back:
The quality of being kind. The suffix -ness makes a noun.
Bahasa Indonesia: kebaikan
Example: Thank you for your kindness today.
cards.say: kindness. The quality of being kind. The suffix ness makes a noun. Thank you for your kindness today.

cards.back:
The state of having no light.
Bahasa Indonesia: kegelapan
Example: We walked home in the darkness.
cards.say: darkness. The state of having no light. We walked home in the darkness.

cards.back:
In a fast way. The suffix -ly makes an adverb.
Bahasa Indonesia: dengan cepat
Example: He ate quickly because he was late.
cards.say: quickly. In a fast way. The suffix ly makes an adverb. He ate quickly because he was late.

cards.back:
A person who paints. The suffix -er means a person who does something.
Bahasa Indonesia: pelukis
Example: The painter drew a picture of a mountain.
cards.say: painter. A person who paints. The suffix er means a person who does something. The painter drew a picture of a mountain.

cards.back:
Giving pleasure. The suffix -able means able to be.
Bahasa Indonesia: menyenangkan
Example: The picnic by the lake was really enjoyable.
cards.say: enjoyable. Giving pleasure. The suffix able means able to be. The picnic by the lake was really enjoyable.

cards.back:
Feeling that good things will happen.
Bahasa Indonesia: penuh harapan
Example: She felt hopeful about the test result.
cards.say: hopeful. Feeling that good things will happen. She felt hopeful about the test result.
